_description: Each entry = one observed failure mode. Load this at session start so you are pre-warned. Add new entries when you discover new failure modes during migration.

entries.failure: Picks first plausible block + variant without diffing live DOM structure against block JS output. Used `cards-grid cards-grid-cta-card` variant for both indication links (text + chevron) AND glacier patient-support cards (pill buttons) — incompatible inner structures.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule: for every section, capture live block DOM structure and map every class/element BEFORE selecting block.
entries.prevention: Force live DOM inspection in Step 3 of section-fix-prompt. Tag mismatches as 'Variant' or 'Block mismatch' in root-cause taxonomy.

entries.failure: Edited `blocks/brand-explorer/brand-explorer.css` (base, affects all 9 brands) when the fix belonged in `rinvoq-hcp/`. Multiple times treated base CSS as default fix target.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule: lowest-specificity-first cascade not internalized — must be re-asserted in every prompt.
entries.prevention: Step 5 root-cause taxonomy explicitly lists base CSS/JS as ESCALATE-ONLY. First-prompt rule B.5: 'Base block CSS or JS — ESCALATE, do not patch.'

entries.failure: Tried to recreate `section-bg-brushstroke` `gradient--white-glacier` with pure-CSS gradients across 10+ iterations; never downloaded the actual SVG until user demanded.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule: when live uses an SVG, download and reference, do not simulate.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule F.1: 'When live site uses an SVG/PNG, download once to content/content/dam/abbvie-eds-poc/ and reference. Never simulate with CSS gradients.'

entries.failure: Assumed shared header fragment for all rinvoq-hcp pages. Dermatology actually uses different nav items + indication paragraph + active-state styling. Took 30+ turns to discover and fix.
entries.rootCause: Missing context: pharma sites use per-condition headers. No first-prompt rule about discovering header pattern.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule D.1: 'Pharma sites often have per-condition nav and indication text — verify whether shared or sectioned before assuming.' Header fix-loop has fragment-vs-config decision tree.

entries.failure: Abbreviated indications list (dropped PsA + pJIA), dropped 'Limitations of Use', missing entire Boxed Warning section in expanded state, missing 8+ subsections (GASTROINTESTINAL PERFORATIONS, LABORATORY ABNORMALITIES, etc.). Multi-day arc of paraphrasing safety copy.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule (verbatim) + missing context (pharma compliance). Took explicit Step 0 hard-rules prompt with 6 verbatim rules before paraphrasing stopped.
entries.prevention: pharma-content-fidelity skill auto-triggers on safety-bar / ISI text-container / references / dosing blocks. Verbatim rule mandatory. Content diff PRECEDES visual diff.

entries.failure: Wrote desktop-first CSS, patched mobile with `@media (max-width: 985px)` overrides fighting compiled-CSS specificity. Used `0.9rem` (= 9px due to 10px root) instead of `14px` absolute. Hid hero bg on mobile but empty div took 200+ px height. Used `!important` (against project rule).
entries.rootCause: Missing rule (mobile-first) + missing context (10px root font-size) + missing skill (regression-protection workflow).
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule E.1: 'Mobile-first. Use min-width media queries.' Rule E.2: '10px root font-size — use absolute px when matching live.' Rule B.6: 'No !important ever.'

entries.failure: Declared '≥90% match' / 'no regression' before user pointed out homepage hero now had 720px min-height, cards-grid had margin-top: -200px, gap between sections changed. Multiple shared-asset regressions undetected.
entries.rootCause: Missing skill: no built-in regression-protection loop. Match-% guessed visually, not measured.
entries.prevention: section-fix-prompt Step 2: capture baseline BEFORE edit. Step 7: per-fix desktop regression diff at 1440 + 1200. Step 8: cross-page regression sweep on every previously approved page.

entries.failure: Tried to recreate `abbv-container resource-container--gold section-bg-brushstroke gradient--white-glacier`, `abbv-safety-bar-content-maximized`, `abbv-nav-active` literally — renaming local classes to match Platform-C names.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule: class names diverge by design, do not rename.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule A.2 + section-fix-prompt Step 0.1: 'Class names diverge between Platform-C abbv-* and EDS naming. Do NOT rename our classes to match. Match visual and behavioral outcome only.'

entries.failure: Committed and pushed with `git push -u origin` before user said go. Declared 'Pushed successfully' while still failing to recognize regressions. Pasted GitHub PAT in plaintext once.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule: no explicit approval gate before git operations.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule H.1: 'Never git add / commit / push without explicit user approval.' Rule H.2: 'Never declare done without per-viewport screenshots + regression check on other approved pages.'

entries.failure: Recurring 'Brand Explorer has errors! Cannot read properties of undefined (reading fields)'. Flip-flopped between '13 rows' and '10 rows' and 'items need 7 cells' vs '8 cells' for `.plain.html` block tables.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule for xwalk content row count + cell count alignment with model.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule I.1–I.4: 'Parent block = one row per non-tab, non-classes_* field in model order. Item rows = one cell per item-model field. classes_* are NOT rows. Validate row count = model field count before publish.'

entries.failure: Confused gitignored `.plain.html` local-preview content with published AEM JCR content. Hours spent thinking the two were the same.
entries.rootCause: Missing context: `.plain.html` in `content/` is gitignored local-only preview; UE/JCR is separate.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule D.3: '.plain.html in content/ is gitignored local-only preview. AEM / UE / JCR is separate. Never confuse the two.'

entries.failure: 3 H1 tags on homepage hero, no alt text on 10+ images, '+' toggle button without aria-label, single anchor wrapping entire card defeating screen-reader nav. Only caught in Phase D QA.
entries.rootCause: Missing rule: a11y checklist not in first-prompt.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule A.3 + pharma-content-fidelity skill: 'Single H1, alt text on every image, aria-label on icon-only controls, individual links per indication, touch targets ≥44px.'

entries.failure: Brand Explorer items had wrong cell count — removed logoAlt cell when it should be included (8 cells total), and added classes/classes_commonCustomClass as rows when they belong in class attribute only. Flip-flopped between formats because image-text block (no commonProperties tab) skips alt rows but accordion-item (has commonProperties tab) includes them.
entries.rootCause: Inconsistent handling across blocks: blocks WITHOUT commonProperties tab may have server-side alt handling, but blocks WITH commonProperties tab use strict field-per-row/cell mapping for ALL non-tab non-classes_* fields including alt text fields.
entries.prevention: First-prompt rule I.5: For blocks with commonProperties tab, ALL non-tab non-classes_* fields are rows/cells including alt text fields. Always validate against working test content (accordion-test.plain.html has 8 cells matching 8 non-tab non-classes_* item fields; cta-button-test has 12 rows matching model).

entries.failure: Edits to shared assets (styles/rinvoq-hcp/_styles.css, _tokens.css, brand block overrides, or shared fragments) made while migrating /dermatology/access silently regressed the already-approved homepage. The orchestrator's Phase D 'cross-viewport + cross-page QA' is end-of-phase advisory — it ran AFTER the regression had been shipped to local preview. No pre-edit gate forced a snapshot of approved pages BEFORE the shared-file edit. No mechanical list of approved pages to verify against.
entries.rootCause: Existing rule was end-of-phase guidance instead of pre-edit gate. No canonical registry of approved pages — Phase D said 'check previously approved pages' but didn't name them or enforce per-file mapping (which file edit → which page must be checked).
entries.prevention: 1) `approved-pages.json` registry in the orchestrator skill — concrete list of pages requiring regression check. 2) Shared-File Inventory in orchestrator SKILL.md — explicit map of file paths whose edit triggers regression check against EVERY approved page. 3) PRE-EDIT GATE in first-prompt.md Section C: before editing any shared file, snapshot every approved page at 1440/390. 4) Section-fix-loop Step 8 references approved-pages.json mechanically. 5) When a page is approved, append to approved-pages.json — future shared-file edits will automatically guard against regression on it.

entries.failure: Made CSS edits one property at a time without dumping live computed styles first. Spent ~30 turns on the formulary section ping-ponging max-width: 900px → 1220px → none → 100% → 100%; max-width: 100% → revert → re-add. Each tweak was reactive to one user comment without re-reading the live computed-style block as a whole.
entries.rootCause: Section-fix-loop Step 3 (side-by-side diff) is advisory — gets skipped under iteration pressure. No procedural mandate to dump FULL computed-styles for ALL section descendants in one pass before writing CSS.
entries.prevention: Section-fix-loop Step 0 hard gate: MUST run `getComputedStyle()` for live + local for ALL section descendants, output a complete delta table, then write ONE consolidated CSS replacement. If a section needs >3 corrective prompts, STOP and re-dump computed styles before any further CSS edit.

entries.failure: User had to explicitly say 'do pixel comparison', 'do screenshot comparison', 'compare with live site', 'scan each and every node' 12+ separate times. Each time aemcoder would do it and find an issue — but the next round it reverted to 'I think the fix is X' without verification.
entries.rootCause: Section-fix-loop's regression-check step is advisory and was skipped between fixes. No mandatory screenshot+computed-style diff per CSS edit.
entries.prevention: Section-fix-loop Step 0 = mandatory live-vs-local screenshot + style dump. NO CSS edit before this step. Auto-invoke on phrases: 'still not', 'not matching', 'still off', 'still broken', 'pixel comparison', 'scan each node', 'fix is limited to', 'do screenshot comparison', 'compare with live', 'still seems broken', 'we have issues', 'Refer the skills'.

entries.failure: ~30 minutes guessing at brand-explorer model format (11 rows vs 8 rows, with/without field hints, `aem-content` vs `reference`, rebuilding compiled JSON) when md2jcr threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading fields)'. Ended with `aem-content` → `reference` change of unclear correctness.
entries.rootCause: Completely uncovered domain. No skill or fix-registry entry documented md2jcr field-collapsing rules, field-hint comment syntax, or the `aem-content` vs `reference` distinction for image fields in container item blocks.
entries.prevention: New 'md2jcr publish rules' section in abbvie-block-analysis: (1) Field-collapsing rules — fields ending in Alt/Text/Title/Type/MimeType become HTML attributes on the parent element, NOT cells. (2) `aem-content` component breaks md2jcr for image fields in item blocks — use `reference`. (3) Required field-hint comment syntax for ambiguous fields. (4) 5-step triage runbook when 'Cannot read properties of undefined' appears: compare working block model, check filter→model chain, verify compiled JSON, check field-component types, dump browser console error stack.

entries.failure: Ran `npm run build:json` and `npm run scaffold:build` which silently recompiled every brand's CSS, polluting the diff with changes to accordion, brand-explorer, cta, footer, formulary-lookup CSS across all brands. User had to flag: 'i am seeing too many changes in other brand level css as well. did we run scaffold:build? if yes, that's wrong, revert' and 'we have unstaged changes in component-*.json files? revert it'.
entries.rootCause: Orchestrator's pre-edit gate covers content files but not build artifacts. No rule about scaffold/build command scope.
entries.prevention: Pre-edit gate Section C addition: Before running ANY `npm run scaffold*` or `npm run build*` command: (1) `git stash` non-target brand files OR use targeted command (`npm run scaffold:build:block --block-name X --brand-name Y` for single brand). (2) After build, `git diff --stat` and verify ONLY the target brand's files changed. (3) Revert any unintended changes to other brands or root component-*.json files immediately.

pages: rinvoqhcp.com regressed during /access migration — second occurrence after AEMCODER-013 supposedly fixed this
entries.failure: Added `.cards-grid-container .cards-grid.cards-grid-cta-card a` rule — affected ALL cards-grid blocks site-wide, broke homepage. Also added `.section.text-container-container .text-container.legal .text-container-text p` — affected all legal text blocks across all pages. AEMCODER-013's pre-edit gate exists but only checks content file scope, not CSS selector scope.
entries.rootCause: Pre-edit gate (AEMCODER-013) checks WHICH FILE is edited, not WHAT SELECTOR is written inside the file. Generic block selectors in styles/{brand}/_styles.css affect every page using that block, but the gate doesn't catch this until visual regression is observed.
entries.prevention: Pre-edit gate addition (CSS selector scope check): Any CSS rule in styles/{brand}/_styles.css touching a shared block class (`.cards-grid`, `.text-container`, `.image-text`, `.hero`, `.formulary-lookup`, etc.) MUST be prefixed with a section-metadata style class (`.section.access-hero-section X`) OR a page-body class (`body.page-access X`). Generic block selectors without a page/section scope prefix are FORBIDDEN — refuse the edit and force re-scope.

entries.failure: Wrote selectors like `.section.hero-container:has(.hero.access-hero)`, `body:has(.hero.access-hero) ...` for ~10 selectors across the migration. Late June 2 user asked 'are you applying section metadata or targeting the .section-wrapper classes directly' — turned out the correct approach was section-metadata `style` class. ALL `:has()` selectors had to be rewritten.
entries.rootCause: Page-templates skill describes recipes but doesn't say 'always introduce a section-metadata style class first and target THAT — never :has() on the block class'. The page-level CSS layer pattern (styles/{brand}/_styles.css uses section-metadata classes) wasn't a procedural rule.
entries.prevention:
Page-templates procedural rule P1: Every custom page section MUST have a section-metadata `style` class authored BEFORE any CSS is written. Authoring: `
style
access-hero-section
`. Selectors in styles/{brand}/_styles.css MUST be of form `.section. ...` and MUST NOT use `:has()` on block class names.

entries.failure: Mobile hero needed 4 layers — (1) skateboarder image on section `::before`, (2) grey brushstroke on `.hero-text-container` `::after`, (3) text on top, (4) `display: block` because parent grid collapsed `::before` to 50px. Each layer discovered separately over ~12 turns. Grid-collapsing-::before issue alone took 4 turns of head-scratching.
entries.rootCause: No skill covers the AbbVie pattern of multi-layered `::before` / `::after` / wrapper-background hero compositions. Layered backgrounds are a recurring pattern across brands but undocumented.
entries.prevention: New 'Layered-background hero recipe' subsection in abbvie-page-templates Hero archetype: BEFORE writing any CSS, inspect live source DevTools and list ALL `::before`, `::after`, parent backgrounds, z-indexes, and parent display-mode constraints (grid collapses pseudo-elements to content-box height — use `display: block` on the section if pseudo-elements need viewport width).

pages: rinvoqhcp.com/dermatology/access — formulary submit button, filter dropdown, plum-circle-vs-cross-button
entries.failure: Added custom search-icon `::before` to formulary submit button. User reported 'now i am seeing two search icon, follow the block library and brand css only'. Same pattern with filter dropdown — added `::before` plum circle + `::after` chevron on top of brand CSS that already had a single `::after` doing both. 3 occurrences before the pattern was internalized.
entries.rootCause: building-brand-blocks documents the cascade hierarchy but doesn't have a procedural pre-read rule. Page-CSS work didn't read existing brand-block CSS before adding decorations.
entries.prevention: building-brand-blocks procedural rule: BEFORE adding ANY `::before`/`::after`/icon rule in styles/{brand}/_styles.css for a block, MUST `Read` both `blocks/{block}/{brand}/_{block}.css` AND `blocks/{block}/{block}.css` to inventory existing pseudo-elements. Do NOT duplicate — override existing rules via CSS variables (if brand block exposes them) or by extending the same selector, never by adding parallel pseudo-elements.

howToAdd: When you discover a new failure mode during migration: 1) Append a new entry with next AEMCODER-NNN id, 2) Set status: 'pending', 3) Once prevention is encoded in a skill, change to 'incorporated-in-skill' and name the skill. The orchestrator skill loads this file at session start so aemcoder is pre-warned about known failures.
